children: At just 16, Jaipur-based changemaker Ariana Agarwal has been recognised for her work to improve the lives of India’s informal workers, receiving the BusinessLine Young Changemaker Award 2026 from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman at an awards function in New Delhi on Tuesday.

The Changemaker Awards, instituted by The Hindu businessline in 2018 to mark its milestone 25th anniversary, recognises individuals, entities and organisations whose work has contributed to materially improving society, the economy and the planet. The Young Changemaker award, an important category, celebrates an individual below 30 years of age.

Ariana’s journey towards bringing about societal change began when she was just a Class 8 student. She noticed that her family’s driver, whom she had known since childhood, did not know his date of birth, did not have a birth certificate and had never seen his Aadhaar card.
“That fact just scared me,” she recalls, saying the experience made her realise how deeply invisibility affected India’s informal workforce.

She began researching issues such as social security, debt and financial literacy, conducting surveys and studying the difficulties faced by informal and gig workers. In June 2024, at the age of 14, she launched the Informal Economy Index (IEI), bringing together volunteers to survey workers and identify their most pressing challenges.

The IEI developed a “vulnerability score” that assesses factors including debt, migration, financial inclusion and access to social protection. Based on the findings, workers are connected with relevant government schemes, financial literacy programmes, debt-management guidance and local support systems. Data is also collated district-wise and State-wise and shared with NGOs and government organisations to support more informed decision-making.

The initiative has directly reached more than 14,000 informal workers across eight to 10 districts in eight States. It has also worked with organisations including Punjab National Bank and ACORN Foundation India. Ariana says the initiative’s larger goal is for institutions to independently adopt and replicate the model.
“I am so happy to win this award as it gives youngsters a seat at the table. It is a strong motivation to work towards achieving the targets set,” she said.

With support from the International Baccalaureate’s Festival of Hope grant, IEI now aims to reach 40,000 workers by the end of the year and evolve from a student-led initiative into a broader systems-change tool.

Ariana’s achievements have continued beyond the informal economy. She also won the Earth Prize 2026 with two teammates for creating Plas-Stick, a low-cost method to remove microplastics from water. Chosen through a public vote of 23,000 people from seven regional finalists, Plas-Stick made the team the first Indian winners of the award.

title: From invisible to included: Ariana Agarwal’s mission for informal workers
